member.name: T:Fable.Core.Py.DecorateAttribute
member.summary: Adds Python decorators to generated classes or methods, enabling integration with Python frameworks like dataclasses, attrs, functools, Pydantic, and any other decorator-based libraries.

remarks.para: The decorator is emitted verbatim. Use importFrom to specify the module to import from.
Multiple [<Decorate>] attributes are applied in reverse order (bottom to top), following Python's standard decorator stacking behavior.
Examples:
[<Decorate("dataclass", "dataclasses")>] - imports dataclass from dataclasses
[<Decorate("lru_cache", importFrom="functools", parameters="maxsize=128")>] - with import and parameters
[<Decorate("app.get(\"/\")")>] - Local variable decorator with parameters (no import needed)

member.name: T:Fable.Core.Py.ReflectedDecoratorAttribute
member.summary: Base class for creating F#-side decorator attributes with access to reflection metadata. Like DecoratorAttribute, but the Decorate method also receives MethodInfo for the decorated member.

remarks.para: Use this when your decorator needs information about the decorated method (name, parameters, etc.).
Example:
remarks.code: type LogWithNameAttribute() = inherit Py.ReflectedDecoratorAttribute() override _.Decorate(fn, info) = Py.argsFunc (fun args -> printfn "Calling %s" info.Name fn.Invoke(args))
remarks.para: Note: This does NOT emit Python @decorator syntax. For emitting Python decorators, use DecorateAttribute or DecorateTemplateAttribute instead.

member.name: T:Fable.Core.Py.DecoratorAttribute
member.summary: Base class for creating F#-side decorator attributes that transform functions at compile time. This is similar to Python decorators but operates during Fable compilation, not at Python runtime.

remarks.para: Inherit from this class and implement the Decorate method to wrap or transform functions.
The decorated function is passed to Decorate, and the returned Callable replaces it.
Example:
remarks.code: type LogAttribute() = inherit Py.DecoratorAttribute() override _.Decorate(fn) = Py.argsFunc (fun args -> printfn "Calling function" fn.Invoke(args))
remarks.para: Note: This does NOT emit Python @decorator syntax. For emitting Python decorators, use DecorateAttribute or DecorateTemplateAttribute instead.
